## Kinetics after the dynamics step (`reactions`) {#sec-ch14-kinetics}

### Summary

Reactions and cloud conversion are not part of snapy's stage loop. A driver calls them once per step, after all
stages, as an operator-split source: it converts the state to concentrations, takes one implicit kinetics step
(@sec-ch06), and adds the resulting density change to the conserved variables. snapy's C++ example drivers and
paddle's `evolve_kinetics` follow the same pattern. Content from source reading only.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $\rho_i \leftarrow \rho_i + M_i\, \delta_i$ per species after the dynamics, @eq-ch14-kinetics-density;
mass @eq-ch14-kinetics-mass; the heat capacity of the Jacobian, @eq-ch14-kinetics-cv.

**Data.** Primitive state in; density change [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$] per species out.

**Placement.** Once per step, after all dynamics stages and before the redo check.

**Activation.** The driver builds `Kinetics` from the `reactions` block of the same input file.

**Guarantee / limits.** Sequential splitting, first order, @eq-ch14-kinetics-splitting; needs the input's rate forms.

**Evidence.** `check_ch14_coupling.py` lines (s) to (w); see the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\delta_i$, concentration change of species $i$ over the step [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$]; $M_i$, molar
mass of species $i$ [$\mathrm{kg\,mol^{-1}}$]; $\rho_i$, partial density [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$]; $q$, the
conserved state of the host model; $\mathcal D$, $\mathcal K$, the dynamics and kinetics tendencies; $\mathsf A$,
$\mathsf B$, linear operators standing for them in the splitting estimate; $S$, the kinetics stoichiometry; $\xi$,
extents per volume; $u_k$, molar internal energy [$\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$]; $c_{v,i}$, isochoric heat capacity per
mole in units of $\mathcal R$ [-], as in @sec-ch14-thermo; $C_V$, $C_P$, volumetric heat capacities at constant volume
and constant pressure [$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$].

### Derivation

The implicit step of @sec-ch06 returns $\delta_i$ in moles per volume. The driver converts it to a partial density
with the molar mass,

$$
\rho_i \leftarrow \rho_i + M_i\, \delta_i ,
$$ {#eq-ch14-kinetics-density}

where $M_i$ enters as the division by `inv_mu`, the inverse molar masses held by `ThermoY`.
@eq-ch14-kinetics-density is computed in the snapy driver, where `inv_mu` divides the change ([`snapy run_hydro.cpp:175-193`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L175-L193)), and in
paddle's `evolve_kinetics` ([`paddle evolve_kinetics.py:7-65`](https://github.com/elijah-mullens/paddle/blob/a4cac94451ab5fc800735edb00180e98859a20c2/paddle/evolve_kinetics.py#L7-L65)).

**Concentrations in.** The driver takes $T$ from its equation of state, the mole fractions from `Y->X`
(@eq-ch14-thermo-mole) and the concentrations from `TPX->V`, then slices off the dry column
([`snapy run_hydro.cpp:176-184`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L176-L184)). For a gas, `TPX->V` returns $x_i\, p/(\mathcal R T)$ divided by the gas
fraction, and with $p$ from @eq-ch14-thermo-pressure this is $\rho_i/\mu_i$: the ideal-gas law closes the loop, so
the kinetics sees the concentrations of @sec-ch14-thermo.

**Mass out.** The implicit step returns a stoichiometric change, $\delta = S\xi$ (@sec-ch06-implicit), so

$$
\sum_i M_i\, \delta_i = \sum_j \xi_j \sum_i M_i S_{ij} = 0 \quad [\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}]
$$ {#eq-ch14-kinetics-mass}

whenever every reaction keeps the molar mass, the condition of @eq-ch14-saturation-mass. The change comes from
`evolve_implicit` ({{< code src/kinetics/evolve_implicit_dispatch.cpp evolve_implicit >}}). @eq-ch14-kinetics-density
then conserves the total density. The dry row is not a kinetics species and stays as it is.

**Energy held.** The driver does not touch $E$, so the hand-back is at fixed $U$: the latent heat of the converted
mass stays in the offsets of @eq-ch14-thermo-energy and appears as a temperature change at the next `VU->T` of the
equation of state. The implicit step itself is isothermal at the pins: without `evolve_temperature` (default false)
`forward_with_rate_constants` returns no temperature derivative
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}}), so the Jacobian has no
temperature column and the rates are evaluated at the driver's $T$ over the whole step. The fixed-$U$ Jacobian of
@sec-ch06-jacobian applies only with that option on (@eq-ch14-kinetics-cv below).

The check feeds the driver's concentrations of the adjusted Jupiter state to these relations.[^ch14-check-kin]

- "(s) gas concentrations from Y->X then TPX->V equal rho_i/mu_i [mol/m^3]: max rel err 4.44e-16 (tol 1e-12) PASS"
- "(t) cloud concentrations from TPX->V against rho_i/mu_i: max rel diff 4.44e-16 (filed as D16; the driver's tendencies start from these) INFO"
- "(u) sum_i M_i delta_i = 0 for a stoichiometric change (mass hand-back): max rel err 2.13e-16 (tol 1e-14) PASS"

<!-- equation-check: eq-ch14-kinetics-mass check_ch14_coupling.py (u) -->

Line (t) is informational: the cloud concentrations agree at these states, and the row D16 it names does not show
there.


**Operator splitting.** The driver solves $\mathrm d q/\mathrm d t = \mathcal D(q) + \mathcal K(q)$, with $\mathcal D$
the dynamics and $\mathcal K$ the kinetics, by applying them one after the other over each step (sequential, or Lie,
splitting): first the dynamics from $q^{n}$ to $q^{\ast}$ over $\Delta t$, then the kinetics from $q^{\ast}$ to
$q^{n+1}$ over the same $\Delta t$. The kinetics never sees the state halfway through the dynamics, and the dynamics
never sees the chemical tendency. For linear operators $\mathsf A$ (dynamics) and $\mathsf B$ (kinetics), the exact
step is $e^{\Delta t(\mathsf A + \mathsf B)}$ and the split step is $e^{\Delta t \mathsf B} e^{\Delta t \mathsf A}$.
Expanding both to second order:

$$
\begin{aligned}
e^{\Delta t(\mathsf A + \mathsf B)} &= \mathsf I + \Delta t(\mathsf A + \mathsf B)
+ \tfrac12 \Delta t^2 (\mathsf A^2 + \mathsf A\mathsf B + \mathsf B\mathsf A + \mathsf B^2) + O(\Delta t^3), \\
e^{\Delta t \mathsf B} e^{\Delta t \mathsf A} &= \mathsf I + \Delta t(\mathsf A + \mathsf B)
+ \tfrac12 \Delta t^2 (\mathsf A^2 + 2\mathsf B\mathsf A + \mathsf B^2) + O(\Delta t^3), \\
e^{\Delta t \mathsf B} e^{\Delta t \mathsf A} - e^{\Delta t(\mathsf A + \mathsf B)} &=
\tfrac12 \Delta t^2 (\mathsf B\mathsf A - \mathsf A\mathsf B) + O(\Delta t^3) .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch14-kinetics-splitting}

The drivers apply the sequence literally: all dynamics stages, each a `forward` of the mesh block
([`snapy run_hydro.cpp:167-168`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L167-L168)), then one kinetics step. The local error is second order and proportional to the commutator $[\mathsf B, \mathsf A]$; summed over
$t/\Delta t$ steps it gives a global error of first order in $\Delta t$, which vanishes only when the two operators
commute (for example kinetics that do not depend on the state the dynamics changes). The kinetics step itself is
the linearly implicit (backward-Euler) step of @sec-ch06, also first order, so the coupled step is first order
overall. This is a property of the sequence above, derived for linear operators; the size of the splitting error in a
snapy or paddle run is not measured. The check compares the split step with the exact one for random $3 \times 3$
operators:[^ch14-check-kin]

- "(w) split-step local error / dt^2 against [B,A]/2: rel diff 6.32e-03 at dt=1e-2, 6.30e-04 at dt=1e-3 (first order in dt; tol 2e-2 at 1e-2) PASS"

<!-- equation-check: eq-ch14-kinetics-splitting check_ch14_coupling.py (w) -->

**Which heat capacity the Jacobian needs.** The temperature term of the Jacobian divides by a volumetric heat
capacity, `jac -= P_j dk/dT u_k / cvol` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::jacobian >}}). It is
derived at fixed internal energy (@sec-ch06-jacobian). In a closed cell at fixed volume, $U = \sum_i c_i u_i(T)$ over
all thermodynamic species, and the kinetics changes only its own species $k$, so
$\mathrm dU = C_V\, \mathrm dT + \sum_k u_k\, \mathrm dc_k = 0$ and

$$
\left(\frac{\partial T}{\partial c_k}\right)_U = -\frac{u_k}{C_V}, \qquad C_V = \sum_i c_i\, \mathcal R\, c_{v,i} ,
$$ {#eq-ch14-kinetics-cv}

where the sum for $C_V$ runs over all thermodynamic species, the dry gas and the clouds included, while $u_k$ is
needed only for the kinetics species. `cvol` must be this $C_V$, which `ThermoY` returns as `VT->cv`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_cv_vol >}}). $C_P$ belongs to a change at fixed pressure, which a
closed cell at fixed density does not undergo. Both snapy drivers pass `TV->cp` instead
(`cp_vol` at [`snapy run_hydro.cpp:181`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L181), passed to `jacobian` at [`:187`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L187); `cp_vol` at [`snapy jupiter_evap_precip_1d.cpp:250`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/examples/jupiter_evap_precip_1d.cpp#L250), passed to `jacobian` at [`:254`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/examples/jupiter_evap_precip_1d.cpp#L254)),
which makes the feedback term too small by $C_P/C_V$. The check measures that ratio on the adjusted Jupiter state:

- "(v) ratio of the volumetric heat capacity the drivers pass (TV->cp) to the C_V of the fixed-U Jacobian: 1.3845 1.3845 1.3846 1.3869 1.3908 1.3961 EXPECTED-FAIL (S14-1)"

<!-- equation-check: eq-ch14-kinetics-cv check_ch14_coupling.py (v) -->

The term is used only when `rc_ddT` exists, that is with `evolve_temperature` on (default false; it is not a YAML
key, and snapy at its pin never sets it), so the substitution is not reached at the pins. This is suspect S14-1:
real and latent. No row of the kintera defect list covers it, because the call is on the snapy side.[^ch14-s14-1] The same transport-then-chemistry sequence is offered inside kintera by the
operator-split solver of @sec-ch09-newton.

### Numerical method

The driver-level sequence, as written in the run-hydro example (`forward_with_rate_constants`, [`snapy run_hydro.cpp:175-193`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L175-L193)) and in the
evaporation-precipitation example (`forward_with_rate_constants`, [`snapy jupiter_evap_precip_1d.cpp:244-261`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/examples/jupiter_evap_precip_1d.cpp#L244-L261)):

1. run all stages of the dynamics, then the equation of state's `forward`, so that the state includes saturation
   adjustment (@sec-ch14-saturation);
2. compute $T$ from the primitive state, mole fractions with `Y->X`, concentrations with `TPX->V`, and the
   volumetric heat capacity with `TV->cp`;
3. drop the dry species by slicing off the first column of the concentrations;
4. call `forward_with_rate_constants` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}})
   and pass its rate constants to `jacobian` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::jacobian >}});
5. call `evolve_implicit` ({{< code src/kinetics/evolve_implicit_dispatch.cpp evolve_implicit >}}) with the `stoich`
   buffer and the step $\Delta t$;
6. convert by @eq-ch14-kinetics-density and add to the conserved state; then run the redo check.

paddle's `evolve_kinetics` ([`paddle evolve_kinetics.py:7-65`](https://github.com/elijah-mullens/paddle/blob/a4cac94451ab5fc800735edb00180e98859a20c2/paddle/evolve_kinetics.py#L7-L65))
takes six arguments: primitive state, equation of state, `ThermoX`, `ThermoY`, `Kinetics`, and the time step.
It also drops the dry species by slicing, calls `forward_with_rate_constants`, and passes the returned rate
constants to `jacobian` ([`paddle evolve_kinetics.py:42-54`](https://github.com/elijah-mullens/paddle/blob/a4cac94451ab5fc800735edb00180e98859a20c2/paddle/evolve_kinetics.py#L42-L54)).
This supplies the explicit rate constants required by `jacobian` when an evaporating condensate is zero
(@sec-ch06). It still computes the volumetric heat capacity with `TV->cp`; the $C_P$ versus $C_V$ issue below
is unchanged.

The figure of the step is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

snapy's `Scalar` module can hold a `Kinetics` module, built with `KineticsImpl::create` ([`snapy scalar.cpp:41-43`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/scalar/scalar.cpp#L41-L43)), but the line that would read its options with
`KineticsOptionsImpl::from_yaml` is commented out ([`snapy scalar_options.cpp:45`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/scalar/scalar_options.cpp#L45)), so the drivers above build the module themselves.

was found that runs them; this was checked by searching snapy's test list, not by running it.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Version floors. snapy requires kintera 2.6.3 or later (`find_package` in [`snapy CMakeLists.txt:97-104`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/CMakeLists.txt#L97-L104); `requires` in [`snapy pyproject.toml:2-7`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/pyproject.toml#L2-L7)). The Kessler
form and the pressure switch of @sec-ch06 exist at the kintera pin, release
2.6.5, and not in releases 2.6.3 or 2.6.4[^ch14-floor-src]. An input that uses them needs kintera 2.6.5, which the
floor does not enforce. What an older kintera does with these keys is not tested.
:::

paddle at its pin declares `torch>=2.6.0`, `kintera>=2.6.4` and `snapy`
([`paddle pyproject.toml:33-40`](https://github.com/elijah-mullens/paddle/blob/a4cac94451ab5fc800735edb00180e98859a20c2/pyproject.toml#L33-L40)).
These bounds permit the report environment's Torch 2.10.0 and native package pins. The committed setup
checks the installed requirements and exercises the six-argument driver on a small CPU card; this does not
validate a complete coupled CRM simulation.

- The drivers pass $C_P$ where @eq-ch14-kinetics-cv needs $C_V$ (suspect S14-1, latent, line (v)); the derivation
  above settles which one is right.

Open questions, not tested:

- The snapy drivers drop the dry species by slicing off the first column. That agrees with the kinetics species
  list only if every other thermodynamic species is a kinetics species, in the same order.
- paddle's `crm` script calls `evolve_kinetics(block, kinet, thermo_x)` ([`paddle crm.py:73`](https://github.com/elijah-mullens/paddle/blob/a4cac94451ab5fc800735edb00180e98859a20c2/paddle/crm.py#L73)), which does not match the
  six-argument signature of `evolve_kinetics` ([`paddle evolve_kinetics.py:7-65`](https://github.com/elijah-mullens/paddle/blob/a4cac94451ab5fc800735edb00180e98859a20c2/paddle/evolve_kinetics.py#L7-L65)).
